questions.question: How wide is 'status note' for stage one of BK-456 on spec 003?

options.label: IDs + yet + status blocks (Recommended)
options.description: Drop every backlog ID and 'yet'. Also move the current-state blocks out of the spec: BE-021's Known divergences (live and departed bullets), its measured backend tallies and the 266/188 cell counts, BE-029's coverage table, and BE-033's 'not yet met' markers. Each goes to its owning dossier (BUG-255/257/318, ID-245, BK-450/455). Rationale paragraphs that narrate history ('BUG-247 is why', 'used to') stay, with IDs removed, for the prune stage. Test docstrings get re-pointed. Diff of roughly 250 lines.

options.label: Literal: IDs and yet only
options.description: Strip IDs, 'yet' and explicit status phrases ('Tracked as', 'since BK-388') in place. The divergence lists and coverage tables stay in the spec without their IDs. Smallest diff, but those blocks are still project state under Rule 7, so the split PR would carry them.

options.label: Full: also history narrative
options.description: Same as the first option, plus moving out the history and measurement narrative the dossier lists (BE-021 lines 941–1216, the BE-029 ranges): rationale written as history, recorded premises, 'this clause used to'. Closest to the dossier's 'status, history and measurement', but it is a judgement-heavy edit that gets close to the prune stage, and it means rewording.

questions.question: For a departed divergence bullet (BUG-246/247/249/243, already done), where does its text go?

options.label: Its done dossier/trace (Recommended)
options.description: Append the measurement, verbatim, as a dated note in the closed item's dossier, or in its trace if it has no dossier, so nothing measured is lost. The done register stays unchanged.

options.label: Delete it
options.description: The BACKLOG-DONE entries and traces already record what shipped, so the spec text is just dropped. Less churn, but the measured detail in the bullet (e.g. SQLBlob's 14 vs 12 operation frames) may exist nowhere else.

With 'not yet met' gone, BE-033's Refusal timing rule (a pure refusal surfaces at the call) is contradicted by test_a_listing_on_a_terminally_closed_backend_fails_at_its_first_page, which is marked BE-033 + BE-020 and asserts the closed guard fires at the first page. How should this PR resolve it?

options.label: Drop BE-033 from its mark (Recommended)
options.description: The cell keeps BE-020 and gets a one-line docstring saying it pins what ships and BK-454 owns the gap, the same pattern BUG-318's cells use. Spec and marks then agree, and the test body doesn't change.

options.label: Keep the spec's gap marker
options.description: Put back 'The rule is stated here and not yet met' (the table stays moved). Spec 003 keeps one 'yet' and the count goes to 1, not 0, but no test changes. That goes against your 'remove every yet'.

options.label: Leave the contradiction
options.description: Ship it as is and record the conflict for BK-454 to settle. Spec and a marked test then disagree on master, which Principle 5 / 000-process Rule 7 treats as an attribution question someone has to decide.

The branch is 1 commit behind origin/master (c48e500, BK-464: CONTENT-RULES last pass; none of its 7 files overlap this branch's). Rebase before opening the PR?

options.label: Rebase and force-push (Recommended)
options.description: Run `git rebase origin/master`, then `git push --force-with-lease`. No file overlaps, so no conflict is expected, and the PR opens on a current base. Only this session tracks the branch.

options.label: Open the PR as is
options.description: Skip the rebase. GitHub merges cleanly since nothing overlaps, but CI runs against a base that is one commit stale.
